aboutHomage: The name, the colors and the compass pay homage to MyGO!!!!! of BanG Dream!. MyGO-Clash is an unofficial project, not affiliated with Bushiroad or the band.
aboutMotto: “It's fine to be lost — keep going.” The band's motto.
advAgentControlDesc: Lets the mygo-clash ctl command line and AI agents through its MCP server drive the app on this computer
advAppLogLevelDesc: For the app's own log file, which helps when reporting a problem; separate from the core's
advAtRestFile: Profiles and secrets are encrypted, with a key in a file only you can read (no system key store found)
advAtRestSecure: Profiles, subscription URLs and secrets are encrypted with a key kept in the {where}
advCoreModeDesc: In the service when installed (needed for TUN), else as a process of the app
advDiagnosticsDesc: Copy a report without secrets, for bug reports
advLicenseDesc: GPL-3.0. Built on mihomo and MyGo.
advLightAutoDesc: Close the window's web view after it stays hidden, to free memory; the core and the tray keep running
advLightNowDesc: The quick panel and the tray stay available
advLogCleanDesc: Deletes log files older than this when the app starts
advLogSizeDesc: Each file's size, and how many files to keep before the oldest goes
advQuitMsg: The proxy stops, and the system proxy and TUN are turned off until you open the app again.
advRestartAppDesc: Quitting also stops the proxy; restarting brings it back
backupExportMsg: The file is encrypted with a password you choose now; you need it to import the file.
backupImportMsg: Enter the password the backup was exported with, then choose the file.
backupRestoreMsg: Your profiles and settings will be replaced. A backup of the current ones is made first.
connClearClosedMsg: The history of closed connections is deleted. The traffic statistics stay.
connCloseAllMsg: Every connection will be closed; apps reconnect.
connectivityCustomHint: The site is probed through the current proxy with a small file, as in MyIP.
connectivityCustomKnown: This site is on the list
connectivityFavEmpty: Tap ☆ on any site to keep it here
connectivityIpHint: The addresses sites see through the proxy. Different addresses for Chinese and global sites mean the rules split your traffic.
connectivityListResetMsg: Every hidden site and the starting favorites come back; sites you added stay.
connectivitySitesHint: Each site is tested {rounds} times; the figure is the fastest, the bars are the rounds.
connectivityVerdictNoDomestic: Chinese sites don't open: check the direct rules
connectivityVerdictNoGlobal: Global sites don't open: check the node or the rules
connectivityVerdictOk: Chinese and global sites both open
coreErrorHint: The core stopped with an error. Restart it, or check the profile on the Profiles page.
coreStartingHint: This takes a few seconds; the page fills in once it runs.
coreStoppedHint: This page shows what the core is doing, so it needs the core running.
editorAppendHint: Added after the profile's own items.
editorDeleteHint: Items of the profile to remove.
editorLinksHint: Paste share links (vmess://, ss://, trojan://, vless://, hysteria2://…), one per line, or a base64 list
editorParseFailed: No proxies were found in the text
editorPrependHint: Added before the profile's own items: rules here match first.
editorRuleOrder: Rules match from the top; the first that matches decides.
homeCustomizeHint: Cards fill each row on their own; turn them on and off, and put them in order.
homeIpFailed: Could not look the address up.
homeLeaves: Traffic no rule sends elsewhere leaves through here.
homeRulesLine: {rules} rules send traffic to {exits} exits; what none matches goes to {fallback}.
homeTunNeedsService: Install the service to capture all traffic
homeTunOff: Only apps that follow the system proxy use it
homeTunServiceOutdated: Update the service to capture all traffic again
logsLevelHint: The core writes logs at {level} and above; quieter ones never reach this page.
logsSilentHint: The core's log level is Silent, so it writes no logs. Raise it to see them here.
modeDirectDesc: Every connection goes direct; the proxy only listens.
modeGlobalDesc: Every connection goes through the proxy selected in the GLOBAL group.
modeRuleDesc: Rules decide, for each connection, whether it goes through a proxy or direct.
onbCheckBody: See which services get through, and how fast.
onbHomeBody: Open a tile for its details, then on into its page — and back to where you were.
onbMoreBody: Tailscale networking and end-to-end encrypted WebDAV sync wait in the sidebar and Settings.
onbNodeBody: Test the delays and choose an exit — the compass turns to it.
onbTrafficBody: System proxy covers most apps; TUN also catches the ones that ignore it.
onbWelcomeBody: It's fine to be lost — this compass points the way.
profilesAutoUpdateHint: When off, the subscription downloads only when you update it
profilesConvertedTip: A list of share links, turned into a profile
profilesDeleteCurrent: It is in use: the next profile in the list takes its place.
profilesDeleteMsg: {name} and its extensions will be deleted.
profilesDiscard: Your changes have not been saved.
profilesDnsWarn: This profile configures DNS itself. Overriding it may break its proxies or some sites.
profilesEmptyHint: Paste a subscription URL above, or import a file.
profilesInsecureHint: Dangerous: anyone on the path could change the profile
profilesIntervalHint: 0 follows the provider's suggestion, or once a day without one
profilesNameHint: Leave empty to use the provider's name
profilesRollbackMsg: The content before the last update comes back ({n} nodes). Doing it again returns to the current one.
profilesRollbackTitle: Go back to the previous version?
profilesUserAgentHint: Some providers answer according to it
profilesWithProxyHint: For subscriptions blocked on your network
proxiesDirectMode: Direct mode: every connection goes direct. Switch to Rule or Global to use proxies.
proxiesFixedTip: The group stays on the proxy you chose instead of the fastest
proxiesHideDeadTip: Hides nodes whose last test failed; the selected one stays
proxiesHideTip: Hide nodes by name, as a regular expression — x2|x3 hides high multipliers. Empty shows everything.
proxiesNoGroupsHint: The current profile defines no proxy groups.
rulesEditTip: Add or remove rules of the current profile
rulesEmptyHint: The configuration has no rules. Import a profile, or add rules to one.
rulesIntro: These are the rules the core is running. They are matched from top to bottom, and the first that matches decides where a connection goes.
rulesOffCount: {n} rules are off for now; they come back when the configuration reloads.
rulesOffTip: Turns the rule off until the configuration reloads
rulesProvidersHint: Rule providers are lists of rules that RULE-SET rules load from elsewhere. Update them here.
rulesQuickTip: Applies to every profile, above its own rules
rulesTestIntro: Enter a domain, an address or a URL to see which rule it would hit and which proxy it would go through. A name is resolved when a rule needs its address, as when connecting.
rulesTestModeDirect: Direct mode is on: every connection goes direct and the rules are not consulted.
rulesTestModeGlobal: Global mode is on: every connection goes to the GLOBAL group and the rules are not consulted.
rulesTestNoIPs: Not resolved (no rule needed the address)
rulesTestNone: No rule matched; the connection goes direct
rulesTestTip: Find which rule a domain or address hits
rulesUpdateFailed: Could not update the rule provider
rulesetsHint: Add rule sets from the community: the core downloads and refreshes them itself, and they apply to every profile, above its rules
serviceCoreInService: in the service, with the privileges TUN needs
serviceCoreInSidecar: as a process of the app, without privileges
serviceNotInstalled: Not installed. TUN mode needs it.
serviceOutdated: Installed version {v} differs from the app's: update it
serviceOutdatedMessage: The installed service is version {v} and the app {app}, as after the app updated. Updating it asks for an administrator’s password; until then the core runs without privileges, and TUN mode is off.
serviceTunMessage: To capture all traffic, MyGO-Clash installs its system service once; the system asks for an administrator’s password. TUN mode turns on as soon as it is installed.
serviceUninstallMsg: TUN mode turns off, and the core runs as the app again.
settingsAllowLanDesc: Let other devices of your network use the proxy
settingsAppearanceDesc: Change the interface's font, or style it yourself
settingsAutoCheckDesc: Keep the delays of selected proxies fresh
settingsAutoCloseDesc: When the proxy or mode changes, close connections so they reconnect through the new route
settingsAutoDetectDesc: Bind proxy connections to the physical interface, to avoid loops
settingsAutoLaunchDesc: Start MyGO-Clash when you log in
settingsAutoRedirectDesc: Redirect TCP with nftables for better performance
settingsAutoRouteDesc: Add the routes that send traffic to the interface
settingsBuiltinDesc: Make old profiles work with mihomo
settingsBypassHint: Hosts and networks, separated by commas or new lines
settingsChainDesc: The proxies whose name matches go out through the front node or group first; the name takes a regular expression, and a chain that closes a loop is dropped
settingsControllerDesc: Serve the core's API on a TCP port, for web dashboards
settingsCopyEnvDesc: The command that points a terminal at the proxy
settingsDnsHijackHint: Addresses whose DNS queries the core answers, e.g. any:53
settingsDnsLeakDesc: In TUN mode, stops Windows from sending DNS queries to the other adapters, and blocks IPv6 when it is off; a few programs that use a LAN DNS server directly, such as virtual machines, may be affected
settingsDnsOverrideDesc: Apply your DNS settings to profiles; each profile can opt in or out
settingsDnsWarn: Leave this alone unless you know what it does: a wrong DNS setting breaks connections.
settingsExcludeRoutesHint: CIDR ranges that bypass TUN, one per line
settingsFindProcessDesc: Find the process of each connection, for PROCESS rules
settingsFlushDnsDesc: Forget cached DNS answers, or the fake IPs handed out in Fake IP mode, when a site resolves wrong
settingsGeoAutoDesc: The core refreshes the databases itself
settingsGeoIntervalDesc: How often the core updates them
settingsGeoSourceDesc: The profile's own addresses win when it has them
settingsGroupIconsDesc: The icons a profile gives its proxy groups, on the Proxies page
settingsGuardHint: Set the proxy again when another app changes it
settingsHotkeysDesc: Work while the app is in the background
settingsHotkeysHint: Click a shortcut, then press the keys. Backspace removes it, Escape cancels.
settingsInterfaceDesc: Send proxy connections out of this interface
settingsLanAuthDesc: Other devices must sign in to use the proxy
settingsLanAuthHint: This device and its apps skip the password, so the system proxy and TUN keep working. Other devices enter these as their proxy username and password.
settingsLogLevelDesc: What the core writes to the Logs page; lower levels write more
settingsMemoryUsageDesc: Shows the core's memory in the traffic card on Home
settingsNotificationsDesc: Show errors and warnings as system notifications while the window isn't in front; click one to open the related page
settingsOledDesc: Use a pure black background in dark mode: less power and more contrast on OLED screens
settingsOriginsHint: Web pages allowed to call the API, one per line
settingsPacDesc: Set a proxy auto-configuration script instead
settingsPacPlaceholders: %proxy-host% and %mixed-port% are replaced by the proxy's address.
settingsPauseOnBlurDesc: Graphs stop drawing while the window is in the background, saving power; they catch up when you return
settingsPrivateNetworkDesc: Lets web dashboards on public sites reach the controller on this computer
settingsProxyColumnsHint: How many columns of proxies the cards take
settingsProxyHostHint: The address applications reach the proxy at
settingsSilentStartDesc: Open in the tray, without the window
settingsStackHint: Mixed is fast and compatible: the system's TCP, gVisor's UDP
settingsStrictRouteDesc: Prevent leaks around the interface; may break some local access
settingsSystemProxyDesc: Point applications that follow the system's setting at the proxy
settingsTcpConcurrentDesc: Connect to every address of a host at once, keep the fastest
settingsTestTimeoutDesc: A node that takes longer counts as timed out
settingsTestUrlDesc: Fetched through each proxy to measure its delay
settingsTrafficGraphDesc: A small upload and download graph at the bottom of the sidebar
settingsTrayModes: Modes in the first level of the menu
settingsTrayModesDesc: Rule, Global and Direct sit in the tray menu itself instead of a submenu
settingsTraySpeedDesc: Show upload and download next to the icon
settingsTunDesc: Capture all traffic with a virtual network interface
settingsUnifiedDelayDesc: Measure delays without the handshake, comparable across protocols
settingsUwpDesc: Choose which Microsoft Store apps can reach the proxy
settingsUwpDone: Saved: the chosen Store apps can reach the proxy
settingsUwpHint: Windows keeps Store (UWP) apps from connecting to this computer, so they cannot use the proxy. The apps you check are exempted; saving asks for an administrator.
settingsWebrtcGuardDesc: Keeps WebRTC in Chrome, Edge and Brave to the proxy, so pages cannot learn your real IP through STUN. Browsers then show they are managed by your organization; undone when the proxy is off or the app quits
settingsWifiDesc: Once each time the computer joins the network named above: switch the profile, turn the proxy or TUN on or off, set the mode
speedHint: Download and upload through the current node, with Cloudflare's speed test. It uses some 100 MB or more.
statsAppsHint: Traffic is split by app only when process matching is set to Always.
statsClearMsg: All recorded traffic statistics will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
statsEmptyHint: Traffic is recorded while the core runs.
statsExcludeHint: One per line: a domain with its subdomains, an address or range, or process:name
statsExcludeLocal: Leave out the local network and the tailnet
statsPartial: Some days have no detail to narrow by, and are left out
subsQuotaAlert: Warn when traffic or time runs low
subsQuotaAlertDesc: From what the provider reports with each update
subsRollback: Go back when an update breaks the configuration
subsRollbackDesc: If the core refuses a subscription right after it updated, its previous version comes back
substoreHint: The address of your Sub-Store backend, with its path prefix if it has one.
syncChangePassDesc: Other devices keep working; new ones need the new passphrase
syncDisconnectDesc: Stop syncing and forget the credentials on this device
syncDisconnectMsg: The server keeps its data. You can join again with the passphrase.
syncDuplicateTip: Same name and system as another device: most likely this computer before the app was installed again
syncEnabledDesc: When off, nothing syncs on its own; Sync now still works
syncEncryptionDesc: Argon2id passphrase key, XChaCha20-Poly1305 per file, names hidden by keyed hashes
syncEncryptionPlainDesc: The server can read the profiles and settings you sync. To encrypt them, set sync up again in a new folder.
syncExistingPassHint: Enter the passphrase you chose on your first device.
syncFoundPlain: Connected. The folder has unencrypted sync data: you can join it next.
syncFoundVault: Connected. The folder has a vault: enter its passphrase next.
syncHeroDesc: Keep profiles and settings in step across your computers through any WebDAV server: Nextcloud, Jianguoyun, Synology, InfiniCLOUD…
syncHttpWarn: http:// sends your password unencrypted. Allow it only for a server on your own network.
syncJoinPlainHint: This folder's sync data is not encrypted, so joining needs no passphrase.
syncKeyReplaced: Another device replaced the sync key. Enter the new sync passphrase to keep syncing.
syncNewPassHint: Choose a passphrase. It encrypts everything on the server and never leaves your devices; enter it on your other devices to join.
syncNoRecovery: Lost passphrases cannot be recovered: the server's data would be unreadable.
syncNoVault: Connected. A new vault will be created.
syncOnChangeDesc: A few seconds after you change something
syncPasswordHint: An app password, where the service offers one
syncPasswordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved one
syncPlainWarn: Unencrypted, your WebDAV provider or the server's admin can read your subscription links (with your provider tokens) and node passwords. To encrypt later, you will need to set sync up again in a new folder.
syncPoint2: The server sees no names nor contents
syncPolicyDesc: When a profile changed on two devices; settings merge field by field
syncRemoveMsg: The device stops syncing the next time it tries, and its statistics leave the other devices.
syncRemovedBanner: {device} removed this device from sync. Set sync up again to rejoin.
syncRemovedBannerAnon: This device was removed from sync. Set sync up again to rejoin.
syncRevokeBehind: {names} run an older version and will ask for the new passphrase.
syncRevokeDesc: Encrypts the server's data again under a new key, so the removed device can no longer read it, even with the old passphrase
syncRevoked: Removed, and the sync key was replaced
syncTailnetDesc: Devices on the same tailnet sync the moment one of them changes
syncTailnetOff: Turn Tailscale on first; devices on the same tailnet then sync the moment one of them changes
syncTailnetTip: Gets changes over Tailscale at once
syncTransportHttp: Unencrypted HTTP: contents stay encrypted, the password does not
syncTransportPinned: TLS, with the server's pinned key
syncTsNote: Tailscale settings sync; the sign-in follows an auth key shared on the Tailscale page, and each device keeps its own name.
syncUntrusted: Certificate authorities do not trust this server. Trust its key above, if it is yours.
syncUrlHint: The folder the app's own folder goes in
syncWhatDesc: Device-specific settings (TUN, hotkeys, names) never sync
tsAcceptRoutesHint: Use the subnets other devices advertise
tsAuthKeyHint: Recommended: a reusable auth key lets every device sign in as its own device without clashing, and sync can carry it to the others. Generate one in the admin console under Settings › Keys
tsCoexistHint: Send tailnet traffic and names around the proxy, and keep TUN off Tailscale's routes
tsConnectedHint: Connect or disconnect the Tailscale app
tsControlUnreachable: The Tailscale control server is unreachable
tsControlUnreachableHint: Signing in connects to the control server first. Pick a working proxy group under Built-in node › Reach Tailscale through below, then sign in again.
tsControlUrlHint: For Headscale or another server; empty for Tailscale
tsControlViaHint: Where the coordination server and relays are blocked, connect to them through a proxy group
tsDeviceNameHint: How the device appears in your tailnet
tsEmbeddedDesc: MyGO-Clash runs its own Tailscale node, in user space: nothing else to install, no admin rights.
tsEmbeddedP1: Tailnet addresses and MagicDNS names go through a Tailscale outbound, by rules
tsEmbeddedP2: Use exit nodes and subnet routers like any proxy
tsEmbeddedP3: Optionally share this proxy with your own devices on the tailnet
tsEphemeralHint: The device disappears from the tailnet when it goes offline
tsExitHintEmbedded: Internet traffic routed to the Tailscale outbound leaves through this device.
tsExitHintSystem: All internet traffic of this computer leaves through this device.
tsHeroDesc: Reach the devices of your Tailscale network by name, route subnets and exit nodes through your rules, and keep TUN mode from fighting with Tailscale.
tsInstallHint: Install Tailscale and sign in, or use the built-in node instead.
tsJoinSelector: Add to the first selector group
tsJoinSelectorHint: Select {name} like any proxy, e.g. to use an exit node for everything
tsKeyShared: The auth key is shared through sync: your other devices sign in with it, each as a device of its own.
tsLogoutMsg: The device leaves the tailnet and its identity is deleted; signing in again adds a new device.
tsNeedsApproval: This device waits for approval in the admin console.
tsNoExitNodes: No device of the tailnet offers to be an exit node.
tsOffHint: Connect your tailnet to reach your devices through the proxy.
tsRouteSubnetsHint: Add rules for the subnets peers advertise
tsRoutingEmbedded: Rules added before your profile's send these to the {name} outbound:
tsRoutingSystem: Rules added before your profile's send these directly to the Tailscale app:
tsRoutingSystemOff: Coexistence is off: tailnet traffic follows your profile's rules.
tsScanHint: Or scan to sign in from your phone
tsShareKey: Share this key through sync, so my other devices sign in with it (encrypted)
tsShareProxy: Share this proxy on the tailnet
tsShareProxyHint: Your other devices can use this computer's proxy at its Tailscale address; only devices of your account are let in
tsSignInHint: Sign in with your browser, or with an auth key from the admin console.
tsStartingHint: The node is connecting to the coordination server.
tsSystemDesc: Keep using the Tailscale app installed on this computer; MyGO-Clash shows and drives it, and makes the two work together.
tsSystemP1: Tailnet traffic goes direct to the Tailscale interface, bypassing the proxy
tsSystemP2: TUN mode excludes tailnet routes, and MagicDNS keeps working
tsSystemP3: Switch exit nodes and connect from here
unlockHint: Checks what each service allows through your current proxy. Results depend on the selected node.
unlockStale: Tested through another node; check again for the current one
updatesAutoDesc: Look for new versions in the background, and offer them
updatesAutoInstallDesc: Download and install new versions without asking; they take over when the app restarts
updatesPackage: This install can’t update itself: get new versions from the releases page, or from your package manager
updatesReadyDesc: It takes over when the app restarts
wifiApplied: Joined %s: adjusted as the scene asks
